$comment: Haml interpolates #{...} inside its filters, but a filter hands its body straight to another grammar (source.js, source.css, ...). That grammar then reads the { of #{ as its own syntax: in JavaScript it opens an object literal, and a quote inside the Ruby - #{h.fetch('k')} - breaks the recovery, so every following line of the filter is mis-tokenized. Adding the interpolation rule to the filter's own patterns does not help, because TextMate takes the leftmost match on the line and the embedded grammar's rules start earlier; once its begin/end rules are entered, the filter's patterns no longer apply inside them. An injection is the mechanism that does apply at every level of the scope stack, and the L: prefix gives it priority over the host grammar's rules. The lookbehind keeps \#{ out: Haml renders that literally, in filters as well as in plain text, so highlighting it as Ruby would describe code that never runs.

nested_braces.$comment: Keeps #{ {a: 1} } from ending at the inner closing brace. It needs the end-of-line bound as much as the rule above: while a { inside the interpolation is open, it is the rule on top of the stack and the outer end is never tried.
